title: What’s In My Human Feedback? Learning Interpretable Descriptions of Preference Data

bias_targets.methodology: Using likelihood ratio tests and mixed-effects models to evaluate whether preference coefficients for specific response features (e.g., preference for narrative prose) vary significantly across self-reported annotator age groups in the Community Alignment dataset.

Measuring how annotator country of origin influences preferences for model output features (e.g., traditional choices, environmental sustainability) using a two-stage meta-analysis and likelihood ratio tests.

Evaluating how annotators' self-reported education levels affect their preferences for model responses (e.g., concrete suggestions vs. cultural reflections) by comparing global preference models to group-specific offsets.

Assessing how annotator gender impacts preferences for specific response features (e.g., prioritizing personal well-being or mindfulness) using statistical modeling of annotator-specific preference coefficients.

Analyzing how annotators' political affiliations shift their preferences for model outputs (e.g., environmental sustainability, social relationships) using likelihood ratio tests to find significant coefficient variations.
